Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
100 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast:
A non-tropical gale-force low pressure area centered a few hundred 
miles southeast of the North Carolina coast is producing 
disorganized showers and thunderstorms primarily along its 
associated stationary front. This low is forecast to move northward 
into unfavorable environmental conditions, and development into a 
tropical or subtropical system is no longer expected.

Regardless of the system's status, this large weather system is 
still expected to produce heavy rains, gusty winds, dangerous surf, 
rip currents, and coastal flooding along portions of the southeast 
and mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week. Additional 
information on this system, including Gale Warnings, can be found in 
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, as well 
as products issued by your local National Weather Service forecast 
office.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...near 0 percent.
